tasks.title: Add unit tests for slugify() and truncate() in orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs
tasks.description:
Create exactly one new file, `orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs`, with unit tests for the two pure helpers `slugify(text, max = 40)` and `truncate(text, max)` exported by `orchestrator/util.mjs`. This change is STRICTLY ADDITIVE: one file created, zero files modified.

Read `orchestrator/util.mjs:60-78` first and derive every assertion from that source, not from intuition. Match the idiom of `orchestrator/test/planner.test.mjs:1-5`: ESM, flat top-level `test("...", () => { ... })` calls (no `describe`), and exactly these imports:
  import { test } from "node:test";
  import assert from "node:assert/strict";
  import { slugify, truncate } from "../util.mjs";

truncate() implementation under test:
  if (!text) return ""; if (text.length <= max) return text; return text.slice(0, max) + `\n... [truncated ${text.length - max} chars]`;
Cover: (1) falsy inputs "", undefined, null, 0 each return "" without throwing; (2) text shorter than max returned unchanged; (3) boundary text.length === max returned unchanged with NO suffix; (4) text longer than max returns the exact full string, asserted literally, e.g. assert.equal(truncate("abcdef", 5), "abcde\n... [truncated 1 chars]"); (5) max === 0 with "abc" returns "\n... [truncated 3 chars]" (empty prefix, suffix still appended); (6) multi-line input is sliced byte-for-byte by slice(0, max) with no special newline handling.

slugify() pipeline under test: toLowerCase() -> replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, "-") -> replace(/^-+|-+$/g, "") -> slice(0, max) -> || "objective".
Cover: (1) slugify("Hello World") === "hello-world"; (2) runs collapse and edge dashes trimmed: slugify("  ---Hello,   World!!! ---  ") === "hello-world"; (3) digits survive: slugify("TASK-001 Fix Bug") === "task-001-fix-bug"; (4) already-slug input is unchanged (idempotent for "hello-world"); (5) non-ASCII is DROPPED, not transliterated: slugify("café") === "caf" and slugify("日本語") === "objective" (do NOT assert "cafe"); (6) "objective" fallback for "", "!!!", "---", and for slugify("hello world", 0); (7) default max is 40: slugify("a".repeat(50)) === "a".repeat(40), and explicit max works: slugify("hello world", 5) === "hello".

MANDATORY quirk test (trim-before-slice): truncation happens AFTER the edge-dash trim, so the result can end with "-". For the input "a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u" (21 single-letter words) the untruncated slug is 41 chars, so slugify(...) returns a 40-char string ENDING IN "-". Assert the real value (length 40 and endsWith("-"), or the exact literal). Do NOT assert a re-trimmed value.

Optional: slugify(undefined) / slugify(null) throw TypeError (no falsy guard, unlike truncate). If you include this, use assert.throws(() => slugify(undefined), TypeError) and name the test so it reads as documenting current behavior.

Do NOT encode as tests and do NOT fix: truncate("abc") with max omitted returns "abc\n... [truncated NaN chars]", and a negative max drops trailing chars while reporting an inflated count. Per DEC-003, report these latent quirks in your task summary as technical debt instead.

Tests must be deterministic: no filesystem writes, no network, no temp dirs, no timers, no dependence on cwd or the clock. Importing util.mjs runs findRepoRoot() at module load; that is pre-existing and harmless — do not work around it.

Finish by running `npm test` and `git status --porcelain`; the latter must show exactly one entry for orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs and zero `M` entries.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs exists and is the only file added; `git status --porcelain` shows a single `??`/`A` entry for it and zero `M` entries.

The file imports only `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` plus `import { slugify, truncate } from "../util.mjs";` and uses flat top-level test() calls with no describe blocks, matching orchestrator/test/planner.test.mjs.
`npm test` exits 0; all pre-existing guardrails/planner/routing tests still pass and every new test is reported as passing by the node:test runner.

truncate coverage: "", undefined, null and 0 each return ""; shorter-than-max returns input unchanged; text.length === max returns input unchanged with no suffix; longer-than-max is asserted as one exact full string equal to text.slice(0, max) + "\n... [truncated N chars]" with N = text.length - max; max === 0 on non-empty text returns the suffix with an empty prefix; a multi-line input case is present.

slugify coverage: basic lowercase/space case; collapsed punctuation runs with edge dashes trimmed; digits preserved; already-slug input unchanged; slugify("café") === "caf"; "objective" fallback for empty, punctuation-only and max === 0 inputs; default max 40 via "a".repeat(50) -> "a".repeat(40); explicit custom max.
A test covers the trim-before-slice quirk, asserting the real 40-char result ending in "-" for the 21-single-letter-word input, not a re-trimmed value.
orchestrator/util.mjs, package.json and package-lock.json are byte-identical to HEAD; no dependency added.
Tests are deterministic: no filesystem writes, network calls, timers, cwd or clock dependence; two consecutive `npm test` runs give identical results.
The worker summary reports the latent util.mjs quirks (truncate with omitted or negative max, slugify throwing TypeError on undefined/null) as technical debt, with no change made to util.mjs.
forbidden: Modifying orchestrator/util.mjs or any existing file, including 'obvious' fixes for the documented quirks.
Modifying package.json, package-lock.json, CI config, or existing test files.
Adding dependencies or test frameworks other than the built-in node:test and node:assert/strict.
Creating additional files (helpers, fixtures, snapshots, temp files) anywhere in the repo.
Placing the file outside orchestrator/test/ or naming it without the .test.mjs suffix (it would silently not run).
Asserting wished-for behavior instead of observed behavior — e.g. "cafe" for "café", or a re-trimmed slug without the trailing "-".
Encoding the omitted-max NaN or negative-max truncate quirks as tests.
Adding tests for other util.mjs exports (globToRegExp, matchesAny, globsOverlap, readJson, ...).
Any filesystem, network, timer or clock dependence in the tests.

parallelization_notes: No parallelism: the entire deliverable is a single new file (orchestrator/test/util.test.mjs). Splitting truncate and slugify into separate tasks would force two workers onto identical allowed_files, which is prohibited, and serializing them would add coordination cost for roughly 20 minutes of work. One task, one wave, one worker.
risks: Wishful assertions instead of observed behavior — chiefly slugify's trailing dash after trim-before-slice and truncate's exact suffix wording. Mitigated by requiring every assertion to be derived from orchestrator/util.mjs:60-78 and by making the quirk test mandatory in the acceptance criteria.
Non-ASCII results look wrong at a glance ("café" -> "caf", not "cafe"); a mis-assertion here produces a red suite. Called out explicitly in the task description and forbidden list.

Scope creep into 'fixing' util.mjs quirks, which would violate the strictly-additive constraint and DEC-003. Enforced by allowed_files covering only the new test file plus the `git status --porcelain` acceptance check.

A file placed outside orchestrator/test/ or missing the .test.mjs suffix would not match the npm test glob and would pass silently without running. Mitigated by requiring the new tests to appear as passing in the node:test runner output.
Otherwise very low blast radius: pure functions, no I/O, no shared state, no production code touched.
